questions.question: Which statement best describes advance care planning?
choices: It is only a DNR signature
It is an ongoing process of discussing values, future decisions, trusted decision-makers, and documenting plans that are reviewed as circumstances change
It is only for people expected to die within days
It transfers all decisions immediately to family
questions.explanation: Advance care planning is a continuing values-and-decisions process for all adults; documents support but do not replace informed conversation and review.

questions.question: What is the main difference between an advance directive and a POLST or similar portable medical order?
choices: They are identical
A POLST appoints a financial agent
An advance directive states future wishes or names a proxy, while POLST converts current goals of a seriously ill or frail patient into actionable medical orders
Only healthy adults need POLST
questions.explanation: Advance directives are legal planning documents for adults; POLST programs create portable clinician orders for selected seriously ill or advanced-frailty patients.

questions.question: A patient with a valid DNR develops painful urinary retention. What is the safest interpretation?
choices: Treat the retention and clarify broader goals because DNR applies to CPR after arrest, not all medical care
Provide no treatment
Assume DNI and do-not-hospitalize automatically
Cancel all medications
questions.explanation: DNR limits attempted resuscitation after cardiopulmonary arrest; other evaluation and treatment continue according to the patient's goals and orders.

questions.question: Which statement about palliative care is correct?
choices: It begins only after all disease treatment stops
It is limited to cancer
It requires a six-month prognosis
It can be provided at any serious-illness stage alongside disease-directed treatment
questions.explanation: Palliative care addresses symptoms, communication, psychosocial and spiritual needs, caregivers, and coordination regardless of disease stage or curative treatment.

questions.question: Under the Medicare hospice framework, which general prognosis criterion is used?
choices: Death must occur within exactly thirty days
A prognosis of six months or less if the terminal illness follows its normal course, with recertification when eligibility continues
Any person over age 65 qualifies
Only metastatic cancer qualifies
questions.explanation: Hospice certification uses an expected prognosis of six months or less under the natural course; it is not an exact countdown and eligibility can be recertified.

questions.question: When a patient lacks capacity, what should guide a surrogate first?
choices: The surrogate's personal treatment preference
The least expensive option only
The patient's known values and prior wishes through substituted judgment, then best interest if wishes are unknown
The loudest relative
questions.explanation: A surrogate represents the patient's voice rather than substituting personal values; best-interest reasoning is used when the patient's preferences cannot be known.

questions.question: What makes a time-limited treatment trial clinically useful?
choices: A defined treatment, duration, outcome targets, burdens, reassessment owner, and plan if targets are not achieved
Starting treatment without discussing when to stop
A promise that recovery will occur
Avoiding documentation
questions.explanation: Explicit targets and stopping rules prevent an uncertain trial from becoming indefinite treatment and connect reassessment to the patient's goals.

questions.question: Which is the best way to communicate uncertain prognosis?
choices: Give an exact date without uncertainty
Avoid discussing it
Ask the family to guess
Ask permission, explain what is known and uncertain, and describe best-case, worst-case, and most-likely trajectories
questions.explanation: Range-based, scenario-based communication is honest about uncertainty and helps patients and surrogates connect decisions to likely outcomes.

questions.question: Which statement about artificial nutrition in advanced illness is most accurate?
choices: A feeding tube always prevents aspiration
Benefits and burdens depend on disease, reversibility, aspiration, fluid status, prognosis, and goals; careful hand feeding may be appropriate in advanced dementia
Declining a tube means declining all feeding
Every hospice patient must stop eating
questions.explanation: Artificial nutrition is a medical treatment with condition-specific tradeoffs; decisions should avoid the false framing of tube feeding versus abandonment.

questions.question: What is the most useful advance-care-planning documentation?
choices: A checkbox that says discussed
Only the diagnosis
Participants, capacity, values, prognosis, benefits and burdens, recommendation, decisions, surrogate authority, forms, distribution, and follow-up
A family member's name without legal or clinical context
questions.explanation: Detailed, accessible documentation allows future teams to understand the patient's voice, the conditions of the decision, and how to implement the plan.
